video.title: Sam Altman's coach destroys your limiting beliefs for 86 minutes straight

summary: My First Million hosts Sean Puri and Shaan interview Joe Hudson, founder of Art of Accomplishment, an executive coach whose clients include Sam Altman and leaders from OpenAI and other AI labs. The conversation covers limiting beliefs, the self-reliance pattern, feeling avoided emotions, visualising worst cases, handling conflict, negative self-talk and running weekly self-experiments. Hudson also describes his path from meditation to VC to coaching. The key business takeaway is that executive coaching and group programmes for founders and exec teams is the one business discussed, and the video is mainly personal-development advice rather than a replicable business playbook.

tactics.name: Weekly self-experiments
steps: Pick a topic you are interested in and read about it.
Design one experiment and run it for a week.
Examples: enjoy what you are doing 10% more five times a day; do only what you enjoy for a week; thank five people a day.
Run a new experiment every few days or weekly.

quote.text: I would read something on that topic and I would design an experiment for myself and I'd run that experiment for a week.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

tactics.name: Hard conversation method
steps: Don't solve the problem for them; ask for a plan, e.g. 'sales are off, present me a plan tomorrow'.
Ask open-ended questions first so they feel heard and you get the full context.
Be vulnerable about your own state ('I feel we've lost trust').
Go in from a service mindset, not fear.

quote.text: I need a plan. Please present it to me tomorrow about how we're going to get sales back on track.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

tactics.name: Visualise worst-case outcomes
steps: Visualise the feared outcome (company failing, divorce) and feel the emotions fully.
Repeat until the fear dissipates; depth of feeling matters more than repetition.

quote.text: It's more until the fear is gone.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

tactics.name: Company health check
steps: Measure how quickly the organisation has hard conversations.
Measure how quickly they resolve them.

quote.text: How quickly do they have the hard conversation? And how quickly do they resolve it?
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

tactics.name: Handle negative self-talk by changing the reaction
steps: Don't try to change the self-talk; change how you react to it.
Run a different reaction experiment each day or two.
List the 20 things the inner voice says most and find seven ways each is untrue.

quote.text: If you try to change the self talk, it's very inefficient. If you change the way you react to the self talk, it's far, far more efficient.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

warnings.warning: Treating self-development as a to-do list for future happiness turns it into a grind and exhausts you.

quote.text: if it becomes like this to do list so that one day you'll be good enough
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

warnings.warning: Failing to be self-aware only works if the environment never changes; when you must change, avoiding it hurts you.
Avoiding conflict in a business means avoiding the places where the system could be improved.

quote.text: every time that we're avoiding conflict in a business, we're looking at a place that we could potentially make the system better
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

lessons.lesson: Effort is rarely why startups fail; relationships and decisions matter more than grinding harder.

quote.text: I've never seen a venture company or a startup fail because of lack of effort.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

lessons.lesson: Avoided emotions such as helplessness drive avoidance behaviours (over-grinding, refusing to delegate) that perpetuate the problem.
Founders with a self-reliance pattern struggle to delegate and ask for help, which limits scaling.
Frame growth as experiments, not failures, so you keep iterating (also applies to sales and marketing).

quote.text: if you frame it as an experiment, then what you're doing is you're constantly learning and you're never failing.
quote.speaker: Joe Hudson

lessons.lesson: Break big goals into the next small win (the piano teacher example) rather than presenting the whole elephant.
Measuring enjoyment at day end is a better efficiency measure than speed because it preserves energy for tomorrow.
Test whether a business is meaningful by asking if you would sell it for a billion dollars and never do it again.
Positive emotions from wins are a muscle; practise feeling them before an exit or you may feel nothing when it comes.
The happiness of the CEO is the key signal of company direction; investors should back a happy founder.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly personal-development opinion and anecdotes from a coach with no figures on his own business revenue, prices or customer counts. Client claims are unnamed and unverifiable. Transcript is Whisper tiny with some mis-heard words.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Joe Hudson sells Art of Accomplishment coaching, courses and The Council programme and plugs his podcast, YouTube and forthcoming book; there is also a HubSpot sponsor read.
